### 4.1 Geographical Scope
This engagement covers Google’s Silicon business operations supporting foundry, OSAT, hub, and warehouse flows within the agreed delivery model. In-scope operating locations include TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL in Taiwan, together with the Google Hub and warehouse locations supporting the Silicon COT supply chain. Delivery will be executed through a hybrid onsite North America and offshore model aligned to the program governance and workstream needs.

### 4.2 Process Scope
In scope are the end-to-end Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain processes required to establish supply visibility, planning control, and execution traceability across foundry and OSAT operations. This includes current-state discovery, fit-gap assessment, and target-state design for constrained supply planning, subcontracting-related flows, forecast and commit visibility, purchase-order collaboration, batch or lot traceability, yield-aware planning, inventory visibility, and supporting master data harmonization. The process scope cuts across production planning, materials management, quality-relevant traceability inputs, and cost or controlling touchpoints to support the improved ASIC commit process.

### 4.3 Technical Scope
Technical scope includes solution design, configuration, and interface enablement across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and agreed boundary systems supporting the Silicon COT model. Bristlecone will leverage Google’s existing integration framework where applicable, including the existing machine-planning integration pattern, and will adapt existing data templates for Silicon planning requirements. In scope are delta integrations using BTP Integration Suite, inbound E2Open capacity and contract manufacturer data into Kinaxis for TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL, resource master integration, yield and unit-of-measure integration, and the definition of data mappings, transformation logic, and validation rules required for phased deployment. Technical ABAP development and analytics build items are limited to requirements confirmed during the Explore phase.

### 4.4 Services Scope
Services included are project management, discovery workshops, fit-gap analysis, to-be process design, business process documentation, functional specifications for approved custom development, configuration and build, test planning and execution, unit testing, system integration testing, user acceptance testing support, regression testing, performance testing, data migration support, cutover planning and execution, go-live support, hypercare, organizational change management, train-the-trainer activities, and knowledge transfer to the support team. The engagement will be delivered in phased Agile execution across Explore, Build, and Deploy.

### 4.5 Application Scope
Application scope includes Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open as the core solution landscape for the Silicon COT supply chain implementation. Within Kinaxis, in-scope capabilities are supply planning, constraint planning, inventory planning, analytics and reporting, and data integration. Within SAP S/4HANA, in-scope capabilities are Production Planning and Materials Management, together with process integration required to support traceability and transaction flows. Controlling-related business participation is expected from Google where required for the COT cost model and associated design decisions.

### 4.6 Integration Scope
| # | Integration | Source System | Target System | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Supply collaboration integration | E2Open | SAP S/4HANA | Supports purchase order, forecast, and commit-message exchanges for foundry and OSAT collaboration. |
| 2 | Planning and execution integration | SAP S/4HANA | Kinaxis | Supports demand signals, WIP snapshots, wafer plan, and planning-relevant execution data. |
| 3 | Capacity and CM data ingestion | E2Open | Kinaxis | Includes capacity information and contract manufacturer data for TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL. |
| 4 | Resource master integration | <CONFIRM: source system for resource master data> | Kinaxis | Supports planning master data required for Silicon planning. |
| 5 | Yield integration | SAP S/4HANA | Kinaxis | Supports yield-aware planning inputs. |
| 6 | Unit-of-measure integration | SAP S/4HANA | Kinaxis | Supports planning and conversion consistency across the solution landscape. |
| 7 | Design BOM / engineering change integration | PLM (Agile) | SAP S/4HANA | In scope for validation during discovery before detailed design is finalized. |
| 8 | Cost, yield, and analytics integration | SAP S/4HANA | BigQuery | Supports analytics and reporting through the Silicon Hub. |
| 9 | Test boundary integration | MES / Test Hub | SAP S/4HANA | Supports unit-level test boundary data; unit-level detailed test data is not included unless separately agreed. |

### 4.7 Exclusions
- Standalone process models outside the Silicon business unit.
- Functionality outside the listed Kinaxis and SAP S/4HANA scope areas unless approved through change control.
- New integration frameworks where the existing Google integration framework can be retained.
- Detailed ABAP development and analytics build items not confirmed after Explore-phase analysis.
- Unit-level detailed test data management beyond the agreed MES / Test Hub boundary integration.
- Work for plants, partners, or warehouse locations not listed in this section.
- Ongoing application managed services, production support, or enhancement services beyond the defined hypercare period.
- Client-owned staffing for controlling activities and client business decisions required for the COT cost model.

- Maintain project governance, status reporting, risk and issue tracking, dependency management, and escalation in line with the agreed governance cadence.

### 12.2 Client Obligations

- Own and provide Finance and Controlling support and any other client-retained capabilities identified as out of scope for Bristlecone.
- Perform client-side testing participation, business validation, UAT sign-off, training attendance, deployment readiness activities, and Go/No-Go decision support through authorized representatives.
- Provide L1 end-user support through Google’s designated business and onsite support teams during hypercare and route escalations to Bristlecone for L2 and L3 handling.

- Approve or reject Change Requests, scope adjustments, and timeline impacts in accordance with the agreed change control process.

### 13.1 Engagement Model
The engagement will be delivered through a fixed monthly commercial model using an onsite and offshore delivery structure aligned to the approved implementation plan. The fixed monthly model covers the agreed delivery capacity for the applicable phase, subject to the defined scope, assumptions, and change control process in this SOW. Phase 3 scaling support will also be billed on a monthly basis, with the final resource load and composition to be mutually agreed based on approved scaling requirements. Any work outside the agreed monthly capacity, approved scope, or project term shall require prior written approval through change control.

### 13.3 Shift Allowance
- No separate shift allowance shall apply unless a non-standard support window is requested and approved in writing.
- Any approved evening, night, weekend, or holiday coverage shall be billed only if expressly agreed before the work is performed.
- Shift coverage required for cutover, hypercare, or critical testing events shall be planned in advance and reflected in the project plan or an approved change request.

### 13.4 Travel & Expenses
Travel and related out-of-pocket expenses shall be billed at actual cost and charged separately from the fixed monthly service fee. Reimbursable items may include accommodation, airfare from the consultant’s base location, local conveyance, visa fees, per diem, travel insurance, and other reasonable project-related travel costs. All travel must be pre-approved by Google in writing before booking. Reimbursement shall be supported by applicable receipts or other reasonable evidence of spend and shall comply with the governing agreement and Google’s applicable travel policy where provided.

### 13.5 Invoicing & Payment Terms
Bristlecone shall invoice Google on a monthly basis for the fixed monthly fees applicable to the relevant phase of the engagement, together with any approved travel and expense reimbursements and applicable taxes. Payment terms shall be as set out in the governing agreement. Applicable taxes shall be charged separately. For Phase 3 scaling support, monthly charges shall apply based on the mutually finalized resource composition and approved capacity for that phase. Any contingency, rate escalation, discount structure, or commercial adjustment reflected in the final pricing schedule shall apply only to the extent expressly approved in the final commercial annex or executed SOW.

### 16.1 Milestone Deliverables Matrix
Milestone deliverables shall be governed against the deliverables defined in Section 9 and the applicable commercial terms in Section 13. The Project Plan and Project Charter, Governance Structure and Engagement Plan, and Risk Assessment and Mitigation Plan establish the execution baseline for Explore. Global Business Process Design, localization outputs, RICEFW and functional specifications, configuration and technical design documents, and integration and data migration deliverables govern transition from design into build. Test scripts and results, training materials, and the Cutover and Go-Live Readiness Package govern deployment readiness. Production Go-Live, Hypercare, and Transition deliverables govern closure of the implementation scope. Where payment milestones are tied to deliverable completion, invoicing shall follow the acceptance and sign-off requirements defined in Sections 9, 11, and 13 rather than elapsed time alone.

### 16.2 Deferred Scope Decisions
- Release 3 scope for additional products, sites, integrations, or capabilities shall be confirmed through governance review and approved through change control before execution.
- The final regional coverage for Release 3 and later phases shall be confirmed in the detailed project plan before those phases are baselined.
- Delta interface scope to be delivered through the existing integration framework and BTP-IS shall be validated during Explore and frozen before build.
- PLM, MES/Test Hub, analytics, and any additional boundary-system scope shall proceed only for approved requirements within the agreed scope and commercial baseline.
- Any ABAP development, analytics build, reports, custom objects, or data conversions not approved after Explore shall remain out of scope unless added through Section 17.

### 16.3 Integration & Custom Code Safeguards
- Only the integrations identified in Section 4.6 are in scope for design and delivery under this SOW.
- Interface design, source-to-target mapping, loading, and validation shall be completed and approved before build or test execution begins for each integration.
- Existing Google integration capabilities shall be retained where applicable; replacement or material redesign is excluded unless approved through change control.
- Custom development shall proceed only for items documented in the approved RICEFW inventory and supported by approved functional specifications.
- Any increase in integration count, new boundary-system connection, or expansion of custom object scope shall require impact assessment for timeline, effort, and commercials before work starts.
- Unit-level test boundary requirements, engineering interfaces, and analytics feeds shall be limited to the approved design baseline for each release.
- Backlog and parking-lot items identified during blueprinting, sprints, SIT, or UAT shall not be treated as committed scope until reviewed and approved through governance.

### 16.4 Change Control
All scope, schedule, deliverable, integration, custom development, staffing-model, and commercial changes shall be managed through the Change Management Process defined in Section 17. No work outside the approved baseline will begin until the change is logged, impact-assessed, reviewed, and approved through the Section 17 process. Approved changes shall be reflected in the project plan, affected deliverables, and applicable commercial terms.

- Bristlecone shall comply with its information security policies and use commercially reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards for the Google data, systems, and environments used under this SOW.

- Google data transmitted or stored by Bristlecone for delivery of the services shall be protected using encryption in transit and at rest in accordance with Bristlecone policy and applicable platform capabilities.

- Bristlecone-managed devices used for the services shall maintain current operating system patching, endpoint protection, and antivirus controls consistent with Bristlecone security standards.

### 19.1 Termination for Convenience
Either party may terminate this SOW for convenience by giving the other party `<LEGAL: required notice period and whether convenience termination is mutual under the governing agreement>` prior written notice.

If Google terminates for convenience, Google will pay Bristlecone for Services performed and approved deliverables completed up to the effective termination date, plus any authorized non-cancellable travel or third-party costs properly incurred before notice of termination. Bristlecone will stop work in an orderly manner, mitigate further cost, and provide transition support for work in progress, open items, and handover materials reasonably requested by Google.

### 19.2 Termination for Cause
Either party may terminate this SOW for cause upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this SOW and fails to cure that breach within the applicable cure period under the governing agreement.

Termination for cause may also occur if a party becomes insolvent, enters liquidation or bankruptcy proceedings, ceases to do business in the ordinary course, or engages in fraud, willful misconduct, or unlawful activity materially affecting this SOW. If Bristlecone is terminated for cause, Google will pay only for conforming Services performed and accepted deliverables completed through the termination date, less any amounts subject to offset under the governing agreement.

### 19.3 Effect of Termination
On termination or expiry of this SOW, Bristlecone will cease the terminated Services as of the effective date, deliver completed work product and agreed in-progress materials for which payment is due, and support knowledge transfer for the period agreed by the parties or otherwise required under the governing agreement.

Each party will promptly return or securely destroy the other party’s Confidential Information, subject to any retention obligation in the governing agreement or applicable law. Termination does not affect payment obligations accrued before the termination date, rights and remedies arising from prior breach, or any provisions that by their nature survive termination, including confidentiality, intellectual property, limitation of liability, indemnity, audit, and dispute resolution, in each case as governed by the governing agreement.
